title: SLO Stakeholder War Room Playbook — Activation, Adoption, and Postmortems
content:
Purpose
- Provide a compact, action-oriented playbook for cross-functional SLO activations and an adoption plan to onboard product and platform teams.
- Focus on: (1) reliably detecting SLO breaches, (2) running a fast, consistent war-room that balances mitigation vs. customer communication, and (3) closing the loop with learning and preventive actions.

Scope
- Applies to latency and availability SLOs owned by Redwood hosted API and Dedicated control plane.
- Includes on-call SREs, serving-runtime, dedicated infra, product-hosted-api, and customer-success where customer-facing incidents occur.
- Excludes low-severity exploratory alerts that map to triage queues (handled by normal pagerflow).

Quick summary of flow (1-2 lines each)
1) Alert triggers SLO breach page in PagerDuty with SLO score snapshot.
2) Initial war-room assembled (SRE + product PM + infra lead) within 15 minutes for P1 SLOs.
3) Short triage (10–15 min): confirm measurement correctness, scope, and customer impact.
4) Mitigate (fallback model, route change, capacity bump) and publish interim status.
5) Post-incident: blameless postmortem with concrete remediation in 10 working days.

Roles & responsibilities (RACI-lite)
- War-room Lead (SRE on-call) — Responsible: assemble responders, keep timeline, drive mitigations.
- Measurement Owner (Telemetry) — Accountable: verify SLO signal integrity, provide historical context.
- Product PM — Consulted: communicate customer impact, prioritize feature rollbacks if needed.
- Infra/Serving Lead — Consulted/Responsible: implement routing or capacity fixes.
- Customer Success — Informed: draft customer comms and coordinate any affected customers.

Pre-launch checklist for an SLO (owner must complete before SLO becomes active)
- [ ] SLO definition doc (intent, user-visible metric, error budget) in Confluence.
- [ ] Measurement source validated with capture-run for 72h comparing raw and derived signals.
- [ ] Alert thresholds mapped to severity (SLO-Breach P1/P2) with PD escalation policy.
- [ ] Playbook links included in the SLO registry row.
- [ ] Runbook per-service with rollback steps and safe mitigations.
- [ ] Stakeholder roster with primary and secondary contacts.

War-room activation checklist (first 30 minutes)
- PD page opens with SLO snapshot and link to the last 90m trace.
- War-room lead pings #sre-war-room and tags product/infra leads. Template: "WARROOM: SLO breach for <service> — lead <name> — join here: <zoom>"
- Measurement owner confirms whether signal is valid; if not, mark as instrumentation incident and escalate to telemetry team.
- Quick scope probe: % of customers affected, regions, model variants.
- Apply fast mitigations in this order (if safe):
  1) Traffic split to fallback model or previous version.
  2) Reduce request concurrency/batching changes for high-latency tails.
  3) Route to alternate region or Dedicated pool if capacity is a cause.
- Publish an interim status note within 25 minutes.

Communication templates (shortest useful)
- Internal (Slack): "STATUS: Incident for <service>. SRE lead <name>. Impact: <short>. Mitigation: <short>. ETA next update: +25m."
- External (CS/Customers): "We’re investigating elevated errors affecting <feature>. We’ve applied mitigations and will share updates at <time>. For urgent questions, contact <cs-email>."

Decision guide for mitigation vs. rollback
- If customer-visible correctness issue -> prioritize rollback of the offending deploy or model version (Product + Serving).
- If latency/resource pressure with no correctness compromise -> scale or route.
- When in doubt, prefer quick rollback if it restores SLO and has low business risk. Document in timeline.

Post-incident (within 72 hours)
- Short blameless summary posted to incident channel summarizing timeline and root-cause hypothesis.
- Owners assigned for containment permanent fix, instrumentation gaps, and SLO definition tweaks.
- Customer communications updated with definitive statement.

Postmortem cadence and output requirements (10-working-day goal)
- Postmortem must include: incident timeline (minute-granular), root cause, contributing factors, remediation plan with owners and ETA, lessons learned, and verification plan.
- Each remediation item must be one of: [automation, architecture change, runbook update, metric improvement].
- Verification: schedule a follow-up audit to confirm behavior improved for the same traffic pattern.

Adoption campaign for product teams (8-week plan)
Week 0: kickoff with SLO fundamentals workshop (SRE + Telemetry + Product).
Week 1–2: Identify candidate SLOs using template; SRE runs capture validation.
Week 3: QA window — compare derived signals to raw.
Week 4: Soft-oncall: product PMs observe real alerts with SRE coaching.
Week 5: Public SLO registry entry goes live in read-only mode.
Week 6–7: Two-week trial where alerts create awareness but do not trigger PD pages (observe-only).
Week 8: Full activation with PD routing and runbook enforcement.

KPIs to measure program health (report weekly)
- Number of services with validated SLOs (target +20 by quarter).
- Mean time to assemble war-room (goal < 15m for P1).
- Fraction of incidents with valid instrumentation (goal > 95%).
- Time-to-remediation (median and 90th).
- % of remediations verified within 30 days.

Dependencies and risks
- Telemetry accuracy: missing or noisy signals will create false war-rooms.
- API/Model rollback friction: lack of fast rollback tooling increases MTTR.
- Cross-team bandwidth: product teams may deprioritize SLO onboarding without clear ROI.

Open questions (to decide in steering group)
- Should we create a dedicated "SLO duty" rotation for product PMs to share operational burden? Pros/cons discussed.
- How do we treat multi-tenant SLOs vs. per-customer SLOs in alerting?

Immediate next steps (owner initials)
- Jordan: draft PD escalation policy and post to Confluence (due 2025-11-18).
- Priya: prototype a signal validation job in telemetry (ENGOPS-412) and run for 72h (due 2025-11-21).
- Alex: prepare the SLO fundamentals workshop deck (due 2025-11-25).

Notes to self / working items
- Keep the war-room checklist intentionally short. Long playbooks stall during incidents.
- Send a quick poll to product leads about their willingness to participate in soft-oncall.
- Add a monitoring dashboard tile that shows live SLO burn rate per service; mobile-friendly.

References
- Confluence: SLO Registry (link above).
- Jira: ENGOPS-412 (signal validation), SERV-RTE-88 (fast rollback tooling).

Version history
- 2025-11-12 initial draft Jordan.
- 2025-12-03 added adoption campaign and KPIs (Priya + Alex).
- 2026-01-17 added war-room communication templates and final alignment notes (Renee).
